summary: A matchmaking episode with an established idol pair, and the comment section behaves unlike anything else on the channel — 3,976 comments on 1.41M views. The second-most-liked comment jokes that she still does not understand and could they please bring the pair back for another hundred episodes, promising to watch a million times herself. Viewers timestamp the single line that broke everyone and note that four million people were destroyed by it. One thread gives specific credit to a host for quickly explaining a puzzle to one guest and defusing a sulk before it started. English-language comments appear discussing how the pair's relationship has grown slowly into something obvious. The channel's own pinned comment asks which couple should be next.

audience_signals: My Ambulove has the highest comment-per-view rate of any series on the channel — roughly seven times the long-form talk average — which makes matchmaking the channel's real engagement engine rather than the flagship flirt show
Idol pairings import an English-speaking international audience that the channel's other talk formats do not reach
The format creates a self-renewing demand queue: every episode's comments name the next pair the audience wants
Hosts are credited as facilitators rather than interviewers here — reading and protecting the guests is the skill the audience values in this format
A single line of dialogue becomes the shareable asset; the audience timestamps it themselves
content_requests: Many more episodes with this pair
Keep asking the audience which couple comes next
